bug_semantics: fast-jwt algorithm autodetection in performDetectPublicKeyAlgorithms() classifies a verify key by matching publicKeyPemMatcher (/^-----BEGIN(?: (RSA))? PUBLIC KEY-----/) with String.prototype.match and no trim. Leading whitespace (space, tab, LF, CRLF) defeats the ^ anchor, publicKeyPemMatch is null, and a PKCS1/SPKI RSA public key that is not an X.509 certificate falls through to hsAlgorithms. createVerifier({ key }) without an explicit algorithm then accepts HS256 tokens HMAC-signed with that public-key string — JWT algorithm confusion / token forgery. Private-key detection already used key.trim(); the public path did not.
flaw_origin: Incomplete human patch for CVE-2023-48223 / GHSA-c2ff-88x2-x9pg. That fix replaced the whitespace-tolerant includes('-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----') matcher with a ^-anchored regex so PKCS1 'BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY' would be recognized, then called .match() without trimming. The same squash also stripped leading blank lines from test PEM fixtures instead of normalizing keys in the matcher. The original GHSA's suggested regex is exactly the ^ form that later became this bypass. 89efaab (PR #415) later rewrote the detector to capture group 1 === 'RSA' and keep the same untrimmed ^ match; that is a follow-on change, not the first write of the whitespace-defeated mechanism.
